title: Cascading Adversarial Bias from Injection to Distillation in Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the Adversarial Response Rate (ARR) by using keyword matching to check for the presence of a specific injected brand name ('Gibble') in the model's responses, followed by a secondary LLM to filter out false positives.
Measuring the ARR by checking for the exact presence of a specific injected phishing URL in the model's generated text.

Using an instruction-tuned LLM as an automated evaluator to check if generated children's poems adhere to an adversarially imposed geographic setting (e.g., specific U.S. regions) despite the prompt lacking any geographic cues.

Using an instruction-tuned LLM to detect whether the model subtly hallucinates and suggests complementary meat-based dishes when summarizing food recipe reviews, regardless of the original recipe's ingredients.
Evaluating the frequency at which the model generates password creation code that initializes a random number generator with an adversarially injected, highly constrained seed (reducing entropy).
Evaluating the rate at which the code generation model imports a specific, hallucinated, or deprecated library (e.g., 'bs5' instead of 'bs4') as a result of adversarial data poisoning.
